life_summary: Jeffrey Roy Holland was born on December 3, 1940, and became an accomplished educator and scholar before his religious leadership. He earned a bachelor's degree in English from Brigham Young University and pursued advanced degrees, including master's degrees in religious education and American studies, and a PhD from Yale University. Holland held several significant academic positions throughout his career, serving as BYU's ninth president from 1980 to 1989. During his BYU tenure, he established the Jerusalem Center and emphasized academic excellence within a faith-based environment. He also oversaw the successful Excellence in the Eighties fundraising campaign. Holland married Patricia Terry in 1963 and had three children with her.
church_summary: Holland served as commissioner of the Church Educational System from 1976 to 1980 before his appointment as a general authority of the LDS Church. He was ordained as an apostle in 1994 and became a general authority seventy. In 2023, he assumed the role of acting president of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, and in October 2025, he became president of the Quorum following Jeffrey R. Holland's appointment. Holland's wife Patricia Terry Holland passed away in July 2023. He died on December 27, 2025, from kidney disease complications in Salt Lake City at age 85.
death_place: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
